overall: Atlanta is tracking well above the NBM forecast at midday, with the running max already at 87.8°F by 12:05 ET and still climbing at a healthy +3.6°F/hr. The warming trend has accelerated noticeably since 11:00 ET (+2.9°F in ~65 minutes), and with roughly 2-3 hours of daytime heating remaining before the typical mid-afternoon peak, conditions are clearly trending hotter than at least one model anticipated. High dewpoint of 71.6°F signals a humid air mass but is not suppressing the temperature rise.
forecast_obs_notes: The NBM forecast of 87.5°F is already obsolete — the running max has surpassed it — while GFS, ECMWF, and HRRR cluster tightly in the 89.9–90.3°F range, showing strong intermodel agreement. The even ensemble model (90–91°F, Tier 1 high confidence) aligns squarely with the primary model consensus, while the odd model's 87–88°F call (Tier 4 Avoid) is effectively busted given current observations.
max_temp_prediction: With the running max at 87.8°F, still ascending at +3.6°F/hr, and 2–3 hours of heating potential left, a final high in the 90–91°F range is the most probable outcome. The three primary NWP models (GFS, ECMWF, HRRR) and the Tier 1 even ensemble all converge on this target, providing solid multi-source support. Confidence is moderately high for a peak near 90.5°F, with the main downside risk being an earlier-than-expected cloud or wind shift that curtails the final 2–3°F of warming.
